See also: Aviso, a viso, and avisó

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
aviso
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish aviso (“advice”). Doublet of advice.

Noun

[edit]

aviso (plural avisos or avisoes)

  1. Advisory; information; advice; intelligence.
    • c. 1638 May 13 (date licensed; Gregorian calendar), Iohn Ford [i.e., John Ford], The Ladies Triall. […], London: […] E. G. for Henry Shephard, […], published 1639, →OCLC, Act I, signature B, recto:
      I am not foot-poaſt, / No pedlar of Aviſo's, no monopoliſt / Of forged Corantos, monger of Gazets.
  2. A kind of dispatch boat or "advice boat", carrying orders before the development of effective remote communication; an advice boat, or dispatch boat.
  3. A mid-sized colonial warship.

Synonyms

[edit]
  • adviso

Translations

[edit]
mid-sized colonial warship
  • Polish: awizo (pl) n, awizowiec (pl) m

Further reading

[edit]
  • “aviso”, in Webster’s Revised Unabridged Dictionary, Springfield, Mass.: G. & C. Merriam, 1913, →OCLC.
  • William Dwight Whitney, Benjamin E[li] Smith, editors (1911), “aviso”, in The Century Dictionary […], New York, N.Y.: The Century Co., →OCLC.
  • “aviso”, in OneLook Dictionary Search.
